name: Blood pressure
why_needed: It helps you notice cardiovascular changes and prepare for posture or landing transitions.
how_to_measure: Use the approved cuff and sit or brace in a stable position.
Keep the cuff at heart level and follow the device prompts.
Record the reading and how you feel.
hazard_effects: Fluid shifts and altered loading can change cardiovascular responses; isolation and delayed support make regular checks useful.
attention: Use your mission medical protocol. If you feel faint, have chest pain, or have a severe or unusual result, contact your flight surgeon.
prevention: Follow your planned exercise, hydration, and landing-preparation routines.
range_note: No clinical threshold is configured in this demo. Follow mission medical standards.

name: Heart rate
why_needed: It gives context about cardiovascular response at rest and around activity.
how_to_measure: Rest in a stable position for the device's instructed interval.
Use the approved sensor or count only if instructed.
Record the number, activity, and symptoms.
hazard_effects: Gravity transitions, workload, sleep loss, and stress can all affect heart rate.
attention: Follow mission limits. Contact your flight surgeon for concerning symptoms or a persistent unusual reading.
prevention: Use scheduled exercise and rest, and report symptoms early.
range_note: No clinical threshold is configured in this demo. Follow mission medical standards.

name: Body temperature
why_needed: It can help identify a change that deserves a repeat check or medical review.
how_to_measure: Use the approved thermometer as its instructions describe.
Measure in the same way each time when possible.
Record symptoms and repeat only as your protocol directs.
hazard_effects: A closed environment can increase exposure to shared microbes; stress and disrupted routines can affect wellbeing.
attention: Contact your flight surgeon for fever concerns or worsening symptoms, following mission protocol.
prevention: Use hygiene and isolation procedures provided by the mission team.
range_note: No clinical threshold is configured in this demo. Follow mission medical standards.

name: Blood glucose
why_needed: It helps track how your body is responding to meals, activity, and health changes.
how_to_measure: Use the approved meter and clean hands as trained.
Follow the device steps and mission schedule.
Record meal timing and symptoms with the value.
hazard_effects: Food availability, workload, sleep, and stress can interact with metabolism.
attention: Use your individual care plan. Contact your flight surgeon for symptoms or results outside mission guidance.
prevention: Follow mission nutrition and hydration plans; do not change treatment based on this demo.
range_note: No clinical threshold is configured in this demo. Follow mission medical standards.

name: Sleep
why_needed: Sleep supports attention, mood, and physical recovery.
how_to_measure: Sync the approved wearable or record your sleep period.
Note interruptions and how rested you feel.
Review the trend with your mission schedule.
hazard_effects: Confinement, workload, and irregular light-dark schedules can disrupt sleep.
attention: Report persistent sleep disruption or problems that affect safe duties to your crew or flight surgeon.
prevention: Keep scheduled downtime and follow mission light-dark routines.
range_note: Educational comparison only; sleep needs vary. Follow mission guidance.

name: Mood and stress
why_needed: A quick check-in can help you notice changes and ask for support early.
how_to_measure: Choose the mood or stress option that best fits right now.
Add a short private note if useful.
Share only through the approved mission channel.
hazard_effects: Isolation, confinement, workload, and communication delay can compound stress.
attention: If you feel unsafe or unable to perform duties, tell a crewmate and contact your flight surgeon now.
prevention: Use scheduled downtime, journaling, privacy, and crew check-ins.
range_note: Self-report is not a diagnosis. Use mission behavioral-health procedures.

name: Exercise
why_needed: It helps you track activity that supports fitness during reduced-gravity missions.
how_to_measure: Sync the approved activity monitor or log a completed session.
Record the activity type and any limitation.
Compare with your mission plan.
hazard_effects: Reduced loading and a closed environment can challenge bone, muscle, and cardiovascular fitness.
attention: Report pain, injury, or a persistent inability to follow your plan.
prevention: Follow prescribed mission exercise routines; adjust only with crew medical guidance.
range_note: No mission exercise target is configured in this demo.

name: Radiation trend
why_needed: A cumulative trend helps crew understand exposure changes and sensor events.
how_to_measure: Sync the mission radiation monitor.
Review the cumulative trend and any event alert.
Follow mission radiation procedures.
hazard_effects: Radiation exposure varies by location and mission conditions; an event can affect the whole crew context.
attention: Follow official mission limits and event procedures. This demo cannot determine allowable exposure.
prevention: Use mission shielding, monitoring, and shelter procedures when directed.
range_note: Relative synthetic trend only. Official limits must come from NASA standards.

name: Symptoms
why_needed: A symptom report gives the crew and flight surgeon context that sensors cannot provide.
how_to_measure: Choose what you are feeling in your own words.
Record when it began and whether it is changing.
Use Help Me Now or contact the flight surgeon when appropriate.
hazard_effects: Multiple hazards can overlap, so symptoms should be interpreted with mission context.
attention: For severe, sudden, or worsening symptoms, alert a crewmate and contact your flight surgeon.
prevention: Use checklists, planned routines, and early reporting; never hide symptoms for a reward.
range_note: No automated diagnosis. Follow mission medical protocols.
